Paul Stone|NORTH TEXAS UNDER 5.5 WINS (+.summary: Stone starts from what left rather than what returns. North Texas won 12 games last season and tied for first in the American before losing the title game 34-21 to Tulane, but head coach Eric Morris and many of the key pieces moved together to Oklahoma State. With just eight percent of their total snaps from a year ago coming back, he finds it difficult to see the Mean Green even breaking even in Neal Brown's first season, and notes an opening stretch of Indiana, UNLV and Texas State they could lose in full. He allows Brown may ultimately succeed in Denton without expecting it this year.
Paul Stone|NORTH TEXAS UNDER 5.5 WINS (+.depends_on: coaching (Morris out, Brown in); returning production — eight percent of snaps; schedule (the opening three)

Pauly Howard|NORTH DAKOTA STATE UNDER 9..summary: Howard's whole case is that the number is too high for a programme that has just changed leagues. He says he is shocked North Dakota State is the third choice to win the Mountain West and carries a win total this high, and that while people are trashing the conference over the teams that have left it, 10-2 remains a big ask.

Jensen Lewis|PARLAY: NOTRE DAME, OHIO ST.summary: Lewis calls this set-it-and-forget-it: barring something ridiculous enough to wreck many other futures on these three programmes, he is backing the sport's top teams to do their job and reach the playoff. On Ohio State he cites returning elite talent in Heisman hopefuls Jeremiah Smith and Julian Sayin, giving Ryan Day a chance at a better overall team than last year's, and adds that the Buckeyes' Over 9.5 team total is a solid foundational future in its own right. On Notre Dame he argues that Marcus Freeman's programme staying independent, and so avoiding a potential SEC or Big Ten gauntlet, is an enormous advantage.

Jensen Lewis|LSU TO MAKE COLLEGE FOOTBAL.summary: Lewis calls Lane Kiffin's arrival in Baton Rouge arguably the most compelling storyline in college football, not just the SEC. He points to a roster overhauled through the portal alongside significant NIL investment, and argues year one under Kiffin usually brings drastic improvement, especially on offense. He expects quarterback Sam Leavitt to run a high-octane attack with fresh receiver transfers around him — big-play threats Jayce Brown from Kansas State and Jackson Harris from Hawaii, plus Winnie Watkins, who followed Kiffin from Ole Miss — and reads the schedule as favourable.

Zachary Cohen|LSU OVER 8.5 WINS (-104 -.summary: Cohen concedes LSU's schedule is hard but stresses that Clemson, Texas A&M, Alabama and Texas all come to Death Valley. Splitting those four should mean 9-3, and he sees a decent chance of 3-1. He argues the Tigers are no longer weighed down by what he calls Brian Kelly's poor coaching, with Lane Kiffin now in the building as one of the sport's brightest offensive minds, Charlie Weis Jr. brought along as coordinator, and Blake Baker — whom he rates among the nation's top defensive coordinators — retained. His conclusion is that this will be a very well-coached team. Note the stake is printed: three units.

At plus money he will take that chance. He calls Kyle Whittingham one of the coaches he trusts most and credits him with retooling the roster quickly, keeping seven offensive starters, and says play-caller Jason Beck should be able to turn Bryce Underwood into one of the most feared quarterbacks in the sport. He argues Wisconsin was trending downward before Luke Fickell arrived — getting beaten by the Big Ten's elite and recruiting poorly — and that Fickell has at least turned the recruiting around, which is part of why he rates the 2026 roster as talented as it is. He also notes there is now NIL money to work with. Stake printed: three units.

He acknowledges hard games — road trips to TCU and Utah, Notre Dame at home — but argues those are exactly the wins the committee wanted to see last year. He expects the Cougars to be highly productive on both sides: LJ Martin, one of the nation's top backs, returns behind an offensive line he calls tremendous, and Bear Bachmeier should improve markedly as a passer in his second year starting.

Ben Stevens|NEW MEXICO TO WIN THE MOUNTA.summary: Stevens leads with Jason Eck, who took the Lobos to nine wins in 2025 — the most by a New Mexico head coach in a first year in programme history. From that team 14 starters return including quarterback Jack Layne, and 63% of last season's production is back, which he says is the second-most among Group of Six programmes and the most in the Mountain West. He treats that level of retention as evidence of buy-in across the programme in the current climate, and notes the reshaped Mountain West gives the Lobos both UNLV, the favourites, and North Dakota State on the schedule.

Ben Stevens|UCLA OVER 6.5 WINS (+110).summary: Stevens states his conviction in deliberately extravagant terms — if there is only one Bob Chesney believer, it is him — and expects UCLA's new head coach to continue from the start the winning he has done at every previous stop and level. He cautions against the search for the next Curt Cignetti, calling Cignetti the anomaly rather than the standard, but says if you wanted a coach in that archetype it is Chesney, who across 16 years as a head coach from Division III to FBS carries a .717 win percentage.

He points to Kentucky investing in the programme, visible in the portal class, with Notre Dame transfer Kenny Minchey stepping in at quarterback; given what Stein did for the college careers of Bo Nix, Dillon Gabriel and Dante Moore, he has little doubt Minchey will be elevated too. He also lists skill additions including CJ Baxter from Texas, Jovantae Barnes from Oklahoma and Nic Anderson from LSU.

He traces the pattern: Cam Ward arrived having averaged 3,484 passing yards and 24 touchdowns over two Washington State seasons, then became a Heisman finalist and the No. 1 overall pick on the back of more than 4,300 yards and 39 touchdowns; Carson Beck followed from Georgia and posted a career-high 30 touchdowns. Mensah is the next in that line.
